cards.title: Hugging Face & Reflection Launch Beam: 501B Open-Weight MoE for Coding and Agents
cards.why_it_matters: A frontier-scale, Apache 2.0 MoE model with 1M context, full RL recipes, and day-0 vLLM/SGLang support is exactly the kind of open-weight drop that reshapes what self-hosted AI research and production deployments can do.
cards.summary: Beam is a 501B-parameter sparse MoE (23B active per token), 52 layers, 256 experts with 8 routed per token. Supports 1M-token context, five reasoning levels, tool calling, speculative decoding, and ships in BF16/FP8/NVFP4. Day-0 support in transformers, vLLM, and SGLang; full-parameter RL via Miles; custom Rust inference harness. Apache 2.0.

cards.title: T2-Z: Test-Time Optimization of Latent Environment Factors for Robot World Models
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on world models and robot agents, T2-Z shows a principled way to adapt to unseen physical or rule-based environment factors at test time using only a handful of interactions — no supervision on what those factors are.
cards.summary: T2-Z adds a learnable environment latent to a robotic world model. Training alternates between optimizing world-model dynamics and optimizing latents from world-prediction error alone. At test time, the frozen world model adapts by optimizing a fresh latent from one or more interaction trajectories. Across 7 simulated and 4 real tasks, object prediction error drops from 15.20 to 7.00 and action success rises from 33.73% to 72.96%.

cards.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Visual Verifier for Structured World Modeling
cards.why_it_matters: Replacing binary reward signals with fine-grained, decomposed verifiers is a live challenge in multimodal RL and world-modeling pipelines — this work directly addresses that with both empirical results and a theoretical comparison of pointwise vs. pairwise paradigms.
cards.summary: OmniVerifier-C1 decomposes complex prompts into sub-components and assigns pointwise continuous scores rather than binary True/False judgments. A Decoupled RL strategy jointly trains sub-question binary judgment and global alignment scoring. The graded verifier outperforms binary baselines in text-to-image settings and on structured world-modeling tasks (Maze, Sudoku). The paper also shows pairwise verification yields more accurate critiques than pointwise when ground-truth images are available.
